[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game model (corrected): The magenta carriage/shaft operates on a 48px lattice. Up/Down move it and push any unthreaded blocks directly in the shaft's horizontal span one row; blocks just beyond the tip are unaffected. Left/Right retract/advance threaded beads and can push an adjacent unthreaded target as a train. A target is only actually threaded/marked (HUD white 2x2 center) when it is at the far-right bead column and a final Right drives the shaft through it to the board boundary. Thus a nearer target requires one Right per 48px push toward the rightmost column, plus one final Right to pierce. To solve reverse rows, first use progressively shorter vertical pushes to put targets on separate staircase rows without threading; then for each goal color: retract existing chain until tip is just left of target, align vertically, push the whole chain/target right until target reaches far-right column, then one extra Right marks it. Threaded beads stay spaced one lattice cell and move with the shaft. Click is irrelevant.

GUIDE:
Core geometry/controls: Up/Down moves the magenta carriage 48 px on the left rail. Left/Right changes the horizontal gray shaft reach by 48 px. Bead centers use the same 48 px lattice; blocks are 32 px wide. The lower HUD shows required bead order; a correct threaded prefix gets white centers.

Horizontal/free beads: advancing a tip that meets a movable free bead pushes it (and contiguous beads) right 48 px. At the right boundary (center x400), one extra Right forces the shaft through the blocked bead. A properly carried/threaded train follows vertical carriage moves. Horizontal grip varies: a newly boundary-caught bead may follow only one horizontal step, while a bead refreshed by vertical motion can remain horizontally carried for several steps; to guarantee release, pull it to the leftmost center x112 and retract once more. A free bead can instead be staged without catching by pushing it from behind.

Vertical collision/pushing: when the shaft moves vertically into a row containing free beads anywhere along its reach, it pushes those beads one 48 px cell in the movement direction; vertical chains propagate the push. This enables remote manipulation: e.g. with a target bead at y216 and a free pusher at y264, moving a bare shaft Up from y312 to y264 pushes the pusher to216 and the target to168, while the shaft itself remains below. Likewise a shaft moving Down from y120 to168 pushes a free bead from168 to216. Threaded beads instead move with the shaft.

Core controls/geometry: Up/Down moves the magenta carriage 48 px on the left rail. Left/Right retracts/extends its horizontal gray shaft by 48 px. Bead centers use the same 48 px lattice; blocks are 32 px.

Extension pushes a free bead/contiguous train outward one cell. A boundary-packed train cannot move; further extensions pierce beads in proximal-to-distal order. Threaded beads normally advance outward with extension and ride inward with retraction. If a threaded train is blocked by a perpendicular shaft/bead, the shaft can slide farther through the anchored train. Retraction packs pierced beads toward the carriage. HUD slot whites are reliable proof of correct-color threading.

Two-needle intersection: a bead held by one shaft is immobilized against the other shaft, allowing the second to pierce it. An approach extension may be needed before the penetrating extension; trust the HUD white. Retracting the first shaft leaves the bead on the second. A crossed/blocked bead can anchor a threaded train.

Moving a horizontal shaft vertically sweeps free beads one vertical cell; moving a vertical shaft horizontally sweeps free beads sideways. Threaded beads follow their carriage.
